items.titleEn: Gold steadies, silver falls as Fed holds rates, two officials favor hike - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold was steady and spot silver prices were weaker in late U.S. trading Wednesday, as the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged while acknowledging persistent inflation and resilient economic activity. The central bank's decision was widely anticipated, but dissenting votes in favor of an immediate increase reinforced expectations that further monetary tightening remains possible before year-end. Renewed Middle East tensions and higher crude oil prices added to inflation concerns, limiting buying interest in precious metals despite a softer U.S. dollar. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,056.80 an ounce, down $2.50, or 0.06%, while spot silver was trading near $53.720, down $0.580, or 1.07%. The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% Wednesday, in a 10-2 decision that highlighted continuing disagreements over the appropriate monetary policy response to elevated inflation. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point increase. The Federal Open Market Committee maintained that economic activity is expanding at a strong pace, with resilient domestic spending, robust capital investment and relatively stable labor-market conditions. Policymakers also acknowledged that inflation remains elevated, leaving the door open to further tightening as additional economic information becomes available. The decision marked another pause in the Fed's tightening cycle rather than a clear shift toward easier monetary policy.

items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – The Federal Reserve announced on Wednesday that the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 in favor of maintaining the policy rate unchanged, as expected by the market consensus. “The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate,” the Federal Reserve said in its statement. “The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.” “Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace,” the statement read. “While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.”
